title: Orihah’s Reign
summary: Orihah judged righteously throughout his long life and begot thirty-one children, including twenty-three sons.

explicit_facts.text: Orihah executed judgment in righteousness all his days, and his days were exceedingly many.
Orihah begot thirty-one children, including twenty-three sons.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Orihah is shown judging in a place of governance.
unspecified_visual_details: Orihah’s appearance, clothing, court, and the identities or ages of the children.

narration.text: execute judgment upon the land in righteousness

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the children’s births as a single event.

title: Kib Succeeds Orihah
summary: Orihah begot Kib in his old age; Kib reigned in Orihah’s stead and begot Corihor.

explicit_facts.text: Orihah begot Kib in his old age; Kib reigned in his stead and begot Corihor.

title: Corihor Rebels
summary: At thirty-two, Corihor rebelled against Kib, settled in Nehor, begot children, and drew many people after him.

explicit_facts.text: At thirty-two, Corihor rebelled against his father and went to dwell in the land of Nehor.
Corihor begot sons and daughters, who became exceedingly fair, and he drew many people after him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Corihor’s departure for Nehor may be shown as a move between places.
unspecified_visual_details: The children’s ages and appearance beyond the description “exceedingly fair”; Corihor’s appearance and the nature of his followers.

narration.text: he rebelled against his father

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Corihor’s motives or a specific confrontation with Kib.

title: The King Taken Captive
summary: A man gathered an army, came to Moron, where the king dwelt, and took the king captive. Moron was near the land called Desolation by the Nephites.
characters: The unnamed man who gathered the army

explicit_facts.text: A man gathered an army, came to Moron, and took the king captive.
The king dwelt in Moron.
The king's captivity fulfilled the saying of the brother of Jared that they would be brought into captivity.
Moron was near the land called Desolation by the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king can be shown being taken captive in Moron, with the army present.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearances of the people and army, the manner of capture, and the appearance of Moron are not specified.

narration.text: where the king dwelt, and took him captive

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The brother of Jared's saying is reported; he is not described as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man or the king from verses outside those supplied.
Do not depict the brother of Jared or his saying as a separate visible event.
Do not invent dialogue or a specific manner of capture.

title: Shule Is Born in Captivity
summary: Kib remained in captivity with his people under Corihor until he became exceedingly old; while still captive, he begot Shule in his old age.

explicit_facts.text: Kib dwelt in captivity, and his people were under Corihor, until Kib became exceedingly old.
Kib begot Shule in his old age while he was yet in captivity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Kib can be shown with infant Shule in captivity.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and conditions of captivity, and the appearance or ages of those present.

narration.text: while he was yet in captivity

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the duration of captivity as a specific number of years.

title: Shule Grows Strong
summary: Shule was angry with his brother, grew strong, and became mighty in judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Shule was angry with his brother, grew strong, and became mighty in strength and judgment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Shule may be depicted as a strong adult.
unspecified_visual_details: The brother’s identity in this verse, Shule’s age and appearance, and the cause of his anger.

narration.text: Shule waxed strong

title: Swords at Hill Ephraim
summary: Shule went to hill Ephraim, made steel swords from the hill for those he had drawn away, armed them, and returned to Nehor to battle Corihor.

explicit_facts.text: Shule went to hill Ephraim and made steel swords from it for those he had drawn away.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Shule can be shown making swords at the hill with followers present.
unspecified_visual_details: The sword-making method, tools, followers’ identities, and their appearance.

narration.text: made swords out of steel

title: Shule Restores Kib’s Kingdom
summary: Shule battled Corihor, obtained the kingdom, restored it to Kib, and then received the kingdom from his father and began to reign in Kib’s stead.

explicit_facts.text: Shule battled Corihor, obtained the kingdom, and restored it to Kib.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A battle between Shule and Corihor may be depicted without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The battle’s course and outcome beyond the stated transfer of the kingdom; the manner of Kib’s bestowal.

narration.text: restored it unto his father Kib

prohibited_inventions: Do not add dialogue, wounds, or a coronation ceremony.

title: Shule’s Rule
summary: Shule judged righteously and spread his kingdom across the land as the people became numerous; he also begot many sons and daughters.

unspecified_visual_details: The kingdom’s boundaries, the people’s appearance, and the children’s identities and ages.

summary: Corihor repented of his many evils, and Shule gave him power in the kingdom. Corihor had many children, including a son named Noah.

title: Shule Rescued
summary: As Noah was about to put Shule to death, Shule’s sons crept into Noah’s house by night and slew him. They broke down the prison door, brought out their father, and placed him upon his throne in his own kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: As Noah was about to put Shule to death, Shule’s sons crept into Noah’s house by night and slew him.
They broke down the prison door, brought out their father, and placed him upon his throne in his own kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons can be shown creeping into the house at night, slaying Noah without gore, breaking down the prison door, and bringing Shule out.

narration.text: broke down the door of the prison

title: Two Kingdoms
summary: Cohor, the son of Noah, built up his kingdom in Noah’s stead. His people gained no more power over King Shule. Shule’s people prospered, and the country was divided into two kingdoms.

explicit_facts.text: Noah’s son built up his kingdom in Noah’s stead.
They gained no more power over King Shule.
The people under Shule’s reign prospered exceedingly and grew great.
The country was divided into the kingdom of Shule and the kingdom of Cohor, the son of Noah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A map could distinguish the two kingdoms without specifying their borders.
unspecified_visual_details: The kingdoms’ borders, settlements, and appearance.
The appearances of Cohor, Shule, and their people.

narration.text: And the country was divided; and there were two kingdoms, the kingdom of Shule, and the kingdom of Cohor, the son of Noah.

prohibited_inventions: Do not introduce a different unnamed son of Noah as the ruler.

title: Prophets Warn the People
summary: During Shule’s reign, prophets sent from the Lord warned that wickedness and idolatry were bringing a curse and that the people would be destroyed unless they repented. The people reviled and mocked them, and Shule judged those who reviled the prophets.

explicit_facts.text: Prophets sent from the Lord prophesied that wickedness and idolatry brought a curse, and the people would be destroyed if they did not repent.
The people reviled and mocked the prophets; Shule executed judgment against those who reviled them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophets may be shown speaking while some people mock them.
unspecified_visual_details: The prophets’ names and appearances, the form of their warnings, and Shule’s specific judgment.

narration.text: they should be destroyed if they did not repent

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The curse and destruction are warnings, not events depicted as occurring.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the warned destruction as happening.

title: Shule’s Righteous Rule
summary: There were no more wars during Shule’s days. Remembering what the Lord had done for his fathers in bringing them across the great deep into the promised land, Shule judged righteously throughout his life.

explicit_facts.text: There were no more wars in Shule’s days.

unspecified_visual_details: Shule’s appearance, what prompted his recollection, and any visible sign of remembrance.
